newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan shares flat as Q1 meets expectations.
newsitem.headline: Alcan shares flat as Q1 meets expectations.

text.p: Shares of Alcan Aluminium Ltd were mostly flat on Thursday, as the company released first-quarter results that met analysts' expectations.
After rallying 0.40 earlier in the day, Alcan was up only 0.10 to 43.45 on the Toronto Stock Exchange by late afternoon and unchanged at 31-1/4 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Shares of Alcan, the world's second-largest aluminum producer, have declined more than 3.50 on the TSE since the beginning of April.
Analysts said the company's first-quarter earnings per share of US$0.46 a share, before US$0.16 in special gains, were in line with expectations. A year earlier, Alcan earned US$0.53 a share.
"There is no shock, at first glance," said Manfred Mallory, of Research Capital Corp.
Alcan said it earned a net profit of US$143 million after the gain, in the latest first quarter, versus US$125 million a year earlier. Sales fell to US$1.87 billion from year earlier US$1.99 billion.

Alcan Chief Executive Jacques Bougie said in a statement that the "customer destocking cycle" seen in much of 1996 appeared to have reversed direction, as shown by the company's strong level of shipments and orders in the first quarter.
"Also, prices for fabricated products are beginning to reflect the recent improvement in metal prices," Bougie said.
Alcan's total fabricated volumes in the first quarter rose eight percent from last year's fourth quarter and the year ago first quarter, Alcan said.

But higher volumes in the quarter were offset by lower price realizations for fabricated products, due mainly to a change in product mix caused by business disposals, weaker prices and currency movements, the company said.
Alcan said it was hopeful the improvement in overall business conditions would continue this year.
"While the economy in Europe remains subdued, we are cautiously optimistic that the improved business conditions experienced so far this year will be sustained," Bougie said.
Analysts agreed that Alcan's second-quarter results should improve over the first quarter as higher ingot prices filtered through to fabricated product prices.
"The fabricated prices and ingot prices are better for the second quarter, so it should be better. The second quarter is seasonally stronger," said Tony Hayes, of Credifinance Securities Ltd.
London Metal Exchange aluminum inventories had declined over the last six weeks, Hayes said, a hopeful sign of better times ahead for aluminum prices.
Others agreed that an improvement in European economic growth would help Alcan, which describes itself as the most international of aluminum companies because of its far-flung global operations.

"Europe has been the missing link in the economic scenario. You need a little better sign of growth in Europe than we've had and certainly, there is hope that will be the case," said Research Capital's Mallory.
